Action Plan:
1. Acute widespread eczema flare — prescribe topical mid‑potency steroid (Betnovate) to apply sparingly (fingertip unit) to affected areas twice daily for the next 2 weeks; continue regular emollients (Diprobase) and Dermol in shower; start oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine) — dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript; send prescriptions to Boots pharmacy for collection.
2. Provide patient advice: continue emollients, avoid known irritants, use only small fingertip amounts of topical steroid, stop and seek review for any adverse reaction or allergic reaction.
3. Safety net / follow up: if no improvement after 2 weeks or if symptoms worsen before then (increasing soreness, weeping, fever, systemic symptoms), contact clinic sooner for review; return for reassessment if no response to treatment.
4. Asthma (history) — no change to current asthma management; continue PRN blue inhaler as needed.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Widespread sore, red, very itchy, dry skin over past few days; patient reports acute worsening of chronic eczema.
- Distribution: Chest, hands, arms; worst on the inside of both elbows (antecubital fossae).
- Onset/duration/progression: Acute worsening over the past few days on background of chronic eczema; described as "way worse" recently.
- Symptoms/signs reported by patient: Intense pruritus, dryness, cracking of skin in affected areas; denies weeping/oozing, no visible thickening or scratch marks reported by patient.
- Past medical history: Atopic eczema (chronic), asthma.
- Medications (patient-reported): Emollients — Diprobase; Dermol in shower; OTC topical hydrocortisone (unspecified preparation) — patient reports it did not help; PRN salbutamol (blue inhaler). No current antihistamine in regular use (patient tried an OTC antihistamine previously, reported no benefit — likely cetirizine per conversation).
- Allergies: Patient reports no drug allergies.
- Social/family history: Patient located in London. Mother has hypothyroidism and migraine. Other social history (smoking, alcohol, occupation) not documented.

Objective:
- No clinician-recorded vital signs or formal physical examination documented in transcript.
- Patient-described skin findings: widespread erythema and soreness, dry skin with fissuring/cracks, worst in the inner elbows and hands; no weeping/oozing reported; no systemic features (no fever or joint pains reported).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Eczema flare (acute exacerbation of atopic dermatitis):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Atopic eczema flare (acute exacerbation of chronic atopic dermatitis). (DDx: "Atopic eczema flare (acute exacerbation of chronic atopic dermatitis)" — High likelihood)
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with transcript/DDx):
     - Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis (DDx: Medium) — supporting: acute worsening, involvement of hands/forearms; opposing: patient denied product changes and distribution includes typical atopic sites.
     - Inadequate topical steroid potency / treatment failure (DDx: Medium) — supporting: patient using OTC hydrocortisone and reports no benefit; clinician planned escalation to Betnovate.
     - Secondary bacterial infection / impetiginisation (DDx: Low) — supporting: cracked eczematous skin predisposes to infection; opposing: patient denies weeping/oozing, no fever or systemic signs.
     - Cutaneous T‑cell lymphoma or other chronic dermatosis mimic (DDx: Low) — noted as remote/unlikely given typical distribution and recent acute worsening; consider only if nonresponsive to appropriate therapy.
     - Xerosis / skin barrier dysfunction and irritant contact dermatitis (from DDx) — consistent as exacerbating factors.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Topical steroid: Betnovate (betamethasone — as named in consult). Apply a very small amount (approximately one fingertip unit to cover a palm/back of hand equivalent) to affected areas twice daily for the next couple of weeks (as instructed by clinician).
     - Oral antihistamine: Fexofenadine prescribed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Continue emollients: Diprobase regularly and Dermol in shower; continue current skin care measures.
     - Stop OTC hydrocortisone if escalating to Betnovate (patient previously reported hydrocortisone “didn't work”).
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.
   - Follow-up / safety net: If no improvement after 2 weeks, or earlier if worsening, oozing, increasing pain, fever, or any adverse/allergic reaction to medications, contact clinic for review.

2. Asthma (history):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Asthma — stable per patient report.
   - Differential diagnosis: None applicable from DDx for this visit.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatment planned: No changes — continue PRN blue inhaler as needed.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No clinician-recorded vital signs.
  - No clinician-performed skin examination findings documented (rely on patient description).
  - No medication doses, routes, or full instructions documented for Fexofenadine; Betnovate dose/potency given by drug name and frequency (twice daily) but exact quantity/duration beyond "couple of weeks" not specified.
  - No documentation of pregnancy status (if applicable), smoking/alcohol status, or occupation/possible irritant exposures.
  - No documentation of prior prescription topical steroid potency/duration or adherence details.
  - No photos or objective clinician assessment of infection (e.g., weeping/crusting) recorded.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted — DDx is consistent with the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Generally intelligible; some short pauses and minor inaudible fragments. Key clinical information (symptoms, distribution, treatments prescribed) is documented.
